sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: ERN CONUS LONG WAVE TROUGH WILL UNDERGO CONSIDERABLE INTENSIFICATION THIS PERIOD AS STRONG POLAR JET STREAK DIGS SEWD THROUGH THE NRN PLAINS INTO THE MID MS VALLEY...RESULTING IN STRONG HEIGHT FALLS AND MID TO UPPER-LEVEL LOW FORMATION OVER THE UPPER MIDWEST. MEANWHILE...STRONG VORTICITY MAXIMUM OVER THE OH/TN VALLEYS WILL TEND TO WEAKEN WHILE ROTATING NEWD INTO THE LOWER GREAT LAKES. IN IT/S WAKE...A TRAILING SHORT WAVE TROUGH/VORTICITY LOBE WILL SHIFT EWD THROUGH THE CNTRL/SRN APPALACHIANS TOWARD THE ATLANTIC COAST. IN THE LOW LEVELS...SURFACE CYCLONE NEAR THE IND/OH BORDER AT 20/12Z WILL BECOME DEEPLY OCCLUDED WHILE DEVELOPING NNWWD THROUGH LOWER MI. TRAILING COLD FRONT WILL PUSH EWD THROUGH THE APPALACHIANS TO OFF THE MIDDLE THROUGH SERN ATLANTIC COASTS BY LATER TONIGHT. LATEST MODEL GUIDANCE HINTS AT SECONDARY CYCLOGENESIS ALONG THIS FRONT NEAR THE INTERSECTION WITH RETREATING WARM FRONT WITH THIS FEATURE DEVELOPING NEWD FROM THE CNTRL APPALACHIANS INTO THE DELMARVA BY THIS EVENING.

sections.title: MID ATLANTIC COAST TO NRN FL
sections.text: SCATTERED TSTMS ASSOCIATED WITH ABOVE-MENTIONED OH/TN VALLEY VORTICITY MAXIMUM ARE EXPECTED TO BE ONGOING AHEAD OF SURFACE COLD FRONT AT THE ONSET OF THE FORECAST PERIOD FROM PARTS OF GA AND CAROLINAS PERHAPS INTO VA. WHILE A MARGINAL WIND/HAIL THREAT IS POSSIBLE WITH THIS ACTIVITY THROUGH THE MORNING...IT IS EXPECTED TO DISSIPATE OR MOVE OFFSHORE PRIOR TO MORE SUBSTANTIAL AIR MASS DESTABILIZATION. IN IT/S WAKE...BOUNDARY LAYER HEATING/MOISTENING COUPLED WITH HEIGHT FALLS/DYNAMIC COOLING ASSOCIATED WITH ARRIVAL OF MIDLEVEL VORTICITY LOBE ARE EXPECTED TO CONTRIBUTE TO MODEST AFTERNOON INSTABILITY OVER THE PIEDMONT AND COASTAL PLAIN WITH MLCAPE OF 500-1000 J/KG. TSTMS ARE EXPECTED TO REINTENSIFY AND/OR RE-DEVELOP BY EARLY TO MID AFTERNOON AS COLD FRONT ENCOUNTERS DESTABILIZING AIR MASS. THE PRESENCE OF 50-60 KT SWLY MIDLEVEL FLOW AND A 30-40 KT SWLY LLJ WILL RESULT IN SUFFICIENT /40-45 KT/ DEEP-LAYER SHEAR TO SUPPORT ORGANIZED STORMS INCLUDING SUPERCELLS AND BOWS. HIGH-RESOLUTION DATA SETS SUGGEST THAT STORMS MAY EVOLVE INTO ONE OR MULTIPLE LINES WITH A DAMAGING WIND AND HAIL THREAT SPREADING EWD TOWARD THE COAST BY THIS EVENING. THE POTENTIAL FOR A TORNADO OR TWO APPEARS TO BE THE G

sections.title: OH VALLEY
sections.text: LOW-TOPPED TSTMS ARE POSSIBLE THIS AFTERNOON WITHIN ZONE OF DEEP ASCENT IN LEFT EXIT REGION OF DIGGING UPPER JET. VERY COLD MID LEVEL TEMPERATURES /-26 TO -30 C AT 500 MB/ AND RESULTANT STEEP LAPSE RATES IN CONCERT WITH NWLY UNIDIRECTIONAL WIND FIELDS MAY SUPPORT A FEW STRONGER SHOWERS/TSTMS CAPABLE OF SMALL HAIL AND LOCALLY STRONG WIND GUSTS. ..MEAD/SMITH.. 04/20/2009

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: THE REMNANTS OF THE CLOSED LOW FROM EARLY YESTERDAY IN AR ARE NOW EJECTING NEWD OVER WV/OH...WHILE A SERIES OF UPSTREAM SHORTWAVE TROUGHS DIG SEWD OVER THE MIDDLE AND UPPER MS VALLEY. THIS WILL LEAD TO THE FORMATION OF A NEW/LARGER SCALE CLOSED LOW OVER LOWER MI BY TONIGHT...AND AN UPSTREAM RIDGE WILL PERSIST THROUGH THE PERIOD OVER THE GREAT BASIN. AT THE SURFACE...A COLD FRONT TRAILS SWD TO CENTRAL GA FROM A CYCLONE IN NW OH...AND A WARM FRONT IS LIFTING NWD FROM NC INTO VA. THE COLD FRONT WILL CONTINUE EWD ACROSS THE APPALACHIANS TODAY TO THE ATLANTIC COAST LATE TONIGHT...WITH A WEAK SECONDARY CYCLONE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP AT THE TRIPLE POINT INVOF THE DELMARVA BY EARLY TONIGHT. THE PRIMARY SEVERE STORM THREAT AREA IN THE CONUS TODAY WILL BE FOCUSED NEAR AND E OF THE COLD FRONT THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING FROM THE CAROLINAS NWD INTO THE MID ATLANTIC.

sections.title: CAROLINAS TO THE MID ATLANTIC LATER TODAY INTO EARLY TONIGHT
sections.text: AN INITIAL PRE-FRONTAL BAND OF CLOUDS AND WEAK EMBEDDED CONVECTION IS MOVING NEWD ACROSS CENTRAL NC AND ERN VA IN ASSOCIATION WITH THE EJECTING LEAD SHORTWAVE TROUGH. THIS INITIAL EJECTING WAVE WILL BE FOLLOWED BY ANOTHER SHORTWAVE TROUGH THAT IS MOVING EWD FROM THE MEM AREA ALONG THE MS RIVER. THIS SECOND TROUGH WILL LOOSELY PHASE WITH THE COLD FRONT DURING THE AFTERNOON E OF THE APPALACHIANS... CONTRIBUTING TO A FOCUSED BAND OF ASCENT THAT WILL SUPPORT CONVECTIVE INITIATION ALONG AND E OF THE COLD FRONT THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING. CLEARING IN THE WAKE OF THE MORNING CLOUDS/CONVECTION WILL ALLOW SURFACE TEMPERATURES TO WARM INTO THE 70S NEAR THE FRONT...WHILE BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS WILL SLOWLY INCREASE INTO THE LOWER 60S. THE NET RESULT WILL BE A BELT OF MLCAPE VALUES RANGING FROM 750-1500 J/KG BY MID-LATE AFTERNOON. THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT IS EXPECTED ALONG THE FRONT BY MID-LATE AFTERNOON IN AN ENVIRONMENT OF MODERATE INSTABILITY AND SUBSTANTIAL DEEP LAYER SPEED SHEAR BENEATH A BELT OF 50+ KT MID LEVEL SWLY FLOW. FORECAST HODOGRAPHS ARE SUPPORTIVE OF A BROKEN BAND OF STORMS WITH EMBEDDED SUPERCELLS AND BOWS FROM THE ERN CAROLINAS NWD INTO VA. THESE STORMS WILL BE CAPABLE OF PRODUC

sections.title: MID ATLANTIC STATES INTO NC
sections.text: LATEST SURFACE ANALYSIS SHOWS THE MAIN SURFACE COLD FRONT OVER WESTERN NC/SC...AND A PRONOUNCED MESOLOW NEAR TRI. A WARM FRONT EXTENDS EASTWARD FROM THE MESOLOW INTO SOUTHERN VA. VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY INDICATES BREAKS IN THE CLOUDS ALONG AND NORTH OF THE WARM FRONT...SUGGESTING THAT MODELS ARE CORRECT IN LIFTING THE BOUNDARY NORTHWARD AT LEAST INTO CENTRAL VA BY THIS AFTERNOON. SBCAPE VALUES ALONG AND SOUTH OF THE FRONT WILL RANGE FROM 1000-1500 J/KG WITH DEWPOINTS IN THE 60S. SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO FORM OVER WESTERN NC BY MID/LATE AFTERNOON AHEAD OF THE COLD FRONT. STRONG DEEP LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR WILL PROMOTE SUPERCELLS AND BOWS WITH THIS ACTIVITY AS IT SPREADS EASTWARD. LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH STRONGEST CELLS. BY LATE AFTERNOON...MESOLOW WILL BEGIN TO EMERGE INTO SOUTH CENTRAL VA. LARGE SCALE FORCING IN THIS AREA MAY RESULT IN ISOLATED SUPERCELLS THAT TRACK ROUGHLY ALONG THE WARM FRONT ACROSS VA. IF THIS SCENARIO UNFOLDS...THERE IS AN ENHANCED RISK OF TORNADOES NEAR THE WARM FRONT. OTHERWISE...LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE POSSIBLE. sections.title: GA/SC/NORTHEAST FL
sections.text: MODELS REMAIN CONSISTENT IN DEVELOPING A SECOND AREA OF STRONG CONVECTION THIS AFTERNOON OVER EASTERN GA/SC AND NORTHEAST FL. VERTICAL SHEAR PROFILES AND MODERATE INSTABILITY WILL RESULT IN A RISK OF SEVERE STORMS CAPABLE OF HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS THROUGH THE EVENING. ..HART/JEWELL.. 04/20/2009
